causal_trace.summary: A caller supplies coordinates to Group::from_xy_coordinates.
The API does not enforce that its resulting point lies on the elliptic curve and in the correct subgroup, unlike Group::from_x_coordinate.

The short-Weierstrass affine constructor directly materializes x, y, and infinity without membership checks; the twisted-Edwards constructor instead asserts is_on_curve and panics for an off-curve point.

An invalid short-Weierstrass point can enter later curve operations and could support an invalid-curve attack; the report conditions potential secret revelation on scalar multiplication with secret data. Invalid twisted-Edwards input terminates processing through the assertion.

failure.operation: Unchecked short-Weierstrass affine point construction, or assertion-triggered termination for off-curve twisted-Edwards construction

primary_invariant.statement: A point created from externally supplied coordinates must be validated as on the selected curve and in the correct subgroup before it is admitted as a group element.
primary_invariant.violated_because: Group::from_xy_coordinates lacks those checks; the short-Weierstrass affine constructor returns a point directly, while the twisted-Edwards path uses a panicking assertion rather than fallible rejection.

raw_refs.role: authoritative finding report and reviewed-code excerpts

quality.review_notes: The public audit directly documents the finding, code excerpts, alternative constructor behavior, and recommendation. No historical audited source revision, corrective commit, regression test, PoC, or execution trace is bundled. Secret disclosure is explicitly conditional on later secret-dependent scalar multiplication and is not demonstrated; externally reachable application paths are also not established.

remediation.invariant_restored: Coordinate construction admits a point only after curve and subgroup validation, and represents invalid coordinates as a fallible result rather than a runtime assertion failure.
mitigation_classes: panic-free rejection of invalid external coordinates
